narr: Thunderstorms brought gusty winds to much of Utah and flash flooding to southern Utah.
ev: Flash flooding was reported in the North Fork of the Virgin River. There were two injuries, with search and rescue going into the Narrows to recover those impacted.

Time and location are estimated. A flood wave was observed at the Muddy Creek near Emery gauge, with a rise from around 34 cfs to around 700 cfs between 4:45 and 5 p.m. MDT. This flood wave would have then routed into the warned area between 5 and 6 p.m. MDT.
Time is estimated. A professor of atmospheric science at The University of Utah shared a video showing flash flooding on the East Fork of the Virgin River near Barracks Ranch River Crossing.
Time is estimated. St. George Police reported standing water on I-15 at Washington, milepost 10, that likely led to a rollover accident.
The East Fork Virgin River near Glendale gauge showed two distinct flash flood waves. One at 8:45 p.m. MDT around 145 cfs and one at 10:45 p.m. MDT around 500 cfs.
The Paria River near Kanab gauge jumped from around 15 cfs to 2280 cfs in less than 30 minutes, corresponding to a rise of over 3 ft.
Time is estimated. Hikers were stuck in Paria Canyon and had to be rescued due to elevated river flows.
